prompt: A support organization wants a reusable, reviewed refund-triage Skill only for its support team. Engineering should not inherit it, and the owner needs to update or revoke it later. What distribution plan best fits?

options.text: Install the Skill for every user in the organization and rely on a README to ask engineering to ignore it.
Publish it to a controlled support-team scope with a named owner, versioned release, review path, and documented revoke/update procedure.
Put the Skill text in each support prompt manually so no one needs to manage versions.
Embed the Skill instructions in a shared MCP server credential and distribute the secret only to support.

feedback.reason: The audience is constrained to support and the lifecycle requires change/revocation; distribution scope and version ownership must be explicit.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A Skill is a reusable instruction/workflow asset; its delivery and scope are separate from credentials and live tool authorization.
details.scenarioApplication: The audience is constrained to support and the lifecycle requires change/revocation; distribution scope and version ownership must be explicit.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Exact distribution mechanisms depend on the organization’s supported Claude Code setup; verify behavior before broad rollout.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternatives change a different layer, leave the stated risk uncontrolled, or claim more evidence than the scenario supplies.
details.transfer: Treat reusable assets as owned releases with audience, version, and removal paths.

prompt: A company has a central security Skill that must apply across repositories and be updated by a single owner. Individual teams also have repository-specific build guidance. How should those assets be organized?

options.text: Copy the central security text into every repository and let each project edit its own version.
Place all guidance in one global file without identifying which team owns updates.
Distribute the centrally governed security Skill through the appropriate organization-wide mechanism and keep repository-specific guidance in project scope with clear owners.
Put all guidance in user scope so each developer can decide which security rules apply.

feedback.reason: The intended audience and change authority differ: centrally governed common guidance and project-local instructions need separate ownership/scopes.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Scope should match who needs the asset and who controls its lifecycle.

details.transfer: Separate shared baseline assets from project-specific customization.

prompt: A reviewed Skill was installed across a team, but its instructions now conflict with a changed workflow. The previous version remains in several developer environments. What is the strongest lifecycle response?

options.text: Edit the latest copy only and assume all environments update immediately.
Add a prompt warning that the Skill could be stale, but keep every installed copy active.
Delete the current source and let users keep working with whichever local version they have.
Publish a new reviewed version with compatibility/change notes, define the supported update and removal path, and verify adoption or revoke obsolete copies.

feedback.reason: A source edit does not establish that distributed copies were replaced; version and revocation behavior must be managed and checked.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Reusable assets can become operationally stale, so release state and deployed state need a traceable relationship.
details.scenarioApplication: A source edit does not establish that distributed copies were replaced; version and revocation behavior must be managed and checked.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A staged rollout may be appropriate if old and new versions can coexist safely; define the compatibility boundary.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternatives change a different layer, leave the stated risk uncontrolled, or claim more evidence than the scenario supplies.
details.transfer: Close the loop between asset authorship, distribution, update, and removal.

prompt: A Skill containing internal procedures is being considered for a public community repository. It has no secrets, but the intended audience is currently only the company’s support staff. What should its owner do?

options.text: Keep it in the approved internal distribution scope until the organization reviews disclosure, audience, maintenance, and support implications for public release.
Publish it immediately because the absence of credentials means the procedure has no access risk.
Move it into user scope and tell employees to upload it publicly if they find it helpful.
Encode the procedure in a model prompt so distribution governance no longer applies.

feedback.reason: No secrets does not mean that internal process knowledge is intended for public release; distribution scope is part of governance.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Audience and ownership decisions apply to reusable instructions as well as executable code.
details.scenarioApplication: No secrets does not mean that internal process knowledge is intended for public release; distribution scope is part of governance.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If public release is later approved, remove restricted details and assign external maintenance responsibility.

details.transfer: Match distribution scope to the approved audience and lifecycle.
